clue.text: Malinger? Don't sound well

definitions.meaning: to malinger is to shirk work by feigning illness
to sound a well is to measure its depth with a weighted line; idly twirling that weight instead is the phrase's literal origin

explanation.walkthrough: Sailors meant to take depth soundings with a lead weight on a line; a shirker just swung it about, hence the idiom for dodging work.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to shirk duty by pretending to be ill, which is exactly malingering.

clue.text: Screen' hiding 'ouse in unspecified way

indicators.note: the screening word keeps something concealed within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to screen a film is to show it
a Cockney's dropped-h house is his 'ome, home with no H

explanation.surface: A screen conceals a dropped-aitch house, done somehow or other.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes mark Cockney speech, which drops initial H: the clue's dropped-H house stands for a dropped-H home.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in some manner nobody specifies is a synonym sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Noisy hostelry acquired a valuable bar

indicators.note: noisy means the words before it are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a hostelry is an inn and acquired is got, giving inn got

explanation.surface: A loud pub came into possession of something precious.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast block of gold or silver is a valuable bar of metal.

clue.text: Make hole in exhaust

definitions.meaning: to pierce something is to pass right through it
to exhaust money or supplies is to use them all up, to get through them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to pierce and to use up a stock completely.

clue.text: Feverish from the cold, perhaps, I caught

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the preceding letters may be rearranged into another order

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
taken as written
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Running a temperature after catching a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cold' reads as an illness to fit 'Feverish', but 'perhaps' scrambles it into HECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic is an old medical word for a feverish flush, as in hectic fever.

clue.text: Without originality, hasn't succeeded at first with extravagant style

indicators.note: hasn't says the long word lacks a letter that is taken out

parts.note: copying slavishly is doing it without any originality

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word succeeded

explanation.surface: An unoriginal effort fails to succeed at first, though done in grand style.
explanation.walkthrough: SLAVISHLY loses its S, the first letter of 'succeeded'.
explanation.definitionFit: Done lavishly means done with lavish, extravagant generosity or display.

clue.text: Quarrel when Henry's expelled from school

indicators.note: being expelled from school means one letter is thrown out of the school's name

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public (private boarding) school
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A row breaks out when a boy named Henry is thrown out of school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' looks like a row, but here it is the bolt fired from a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a square-headed crossbow bolt, a kind of missile shot from a bow.

clue.text: Charles invested in simple acquisition

indicators.note: being invested in something means being placed inside it

parts.note: simple means pure, unmixed
Chas is the standard short form of the name Charles

explanation.surface: A man named Charles puts money into an uncomplicated buy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bought is an acquisition, a thing obtained.

clue.text: Don't allow king to stay on board? Just the reverse

definitions.text: to stay on board? Just the reverse

parts.note: to debar is to forbid or exclude
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Refusing a monarch passage on a ship, or the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse' is not a reversal signal: it turns staying aboard into its opposite, leaving the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a ship is the opposite of remaining aboard, i.e. disembarking.

clue.text: Has the potential to become great power

definitions.meaning: a modal verb saying something could possibly happen
strength or force, as in with all one's strength

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the modal of possibility and a noun for strength.

clue.text: Shelter opening after cold start

indicators.note: after places the opening piece behind the single letter
start points to the first letter of the word cold

parts.note: an overture is an opening, as of an opera or negotiations

explanation.surface: A refuge opens following a chilly beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverture is an old word for covering or shelter, also a married woman's legal status.

clue.text: Most Irish characters may appear so unsystematic

indicators.note: the letters may appear in a new arrangement, a signal to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Most of the letters in an Irish word come out at random.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of MOST IRISH are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Done haphazardly, without method, is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: West Indies cricketers joining a — cult

parts.note: CC is a cricket club, a body of cricketers

explanation.surface: Caribbean cricket players join some sect.
explanation.definitionFit: A modern pagan witchcraft religion is a cult in the sense of a system of worship.

clue.text: Close to anger

definitions.meaning: to close a meeting or business is to bring it to an end
to annoy or provoke someone deliberately, in British slang

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to conclude and, colloquially, to tease someone into irritation.

clue.text: Authenticate rumour about Jack

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to noise something abroad is to rumour it
a jack tar, or tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Gossip surrounds a man called Jack, needing verification.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary certifies documents, so to notarise is to authenticate them officially.

clue.text: Engage in flag-waving? That takes the biscuit

parts.note: to flap something is to wave it about
a jack is a ship's flag, as in the Union Jack

explanation.surface: Indulging in patriotism is the last straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for 'that's outrageous'; here the biscuit is the oat bar.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a sweet oat bar baked in a tray is counted a biscuit or traybake.

clue.text: Avoid committing oneself as a cat's-paw

parts.note: a pussy is a cat
an animal's paw is its foot

explanation.surface: Someone dodges commitment by acting as another's dupe.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat's-paw is a dupe, but here it splits into cat and paw.
explanation.definitionFit: To act timidly and noncommittally, treading as softly as a cat.

clue.text: Caught on' film endless time of struggle

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a flick is a film

explanation.surface: Arrested on a never-ending movie, a period of strife.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle or clash is a struggle between opposing sides.

clue.text: Test case in which strikers are confined

parts.note: a Test match is an international cricket game
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A trial in which footballers are kept captive.
explanation.walkthrough: The strikers are not footballers or workers on strike but matches, which strike to light.
explanation.definitionFit: A small container holds matches, which are struck to ignite.

clue.text: King Edward, for example, as lawmaker

definitions.meaning: King Edward is a British potato variety; the slang word for a potato fits
the law that whatever can go wrong will go wrong bears this name

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a potato, and the name attached to the law that anything that can go wrong will.

clue.text: Judge passes sentence that is considerably reduced

indicators.note: the phrase is cut down a good deal, leaving only an inner run of its letters

explanation.surface: A magistrate hands down a much-shortened sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge something is to evaluate or appraise it.

clue.text: Duck in south hard to spot in the air

annotationWithheld.why: Duck in south hard to spot in the air (7): S+TEAL+H gives STEALH; no word gives the T of STEALTH (perhaps 'street' for 'south' in the original), and no scan or search confirms
annotationWithheld.clue: Duck in south hard to spot in the air

clue.text: Victor's wife given a ring

definitions.note: victor is, the 's standing for is

parts.note: the inner is the ring next to the bull on a target

explanation.surface: Victor's wife is given a wedding ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor is one who wins, a champion.

clue.text: Game of highest class between sides from the country

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: between means one piece sits inside the pair of side letters

parts.note: R and L are right and left, the two sides
A is the top grade or class

explanation.surface: Top-class sport played between two teams out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the countryside rather than town, i.e. rustic.

clue.text: This helps to clean up game, supported by sporting body

indicators.note: in a down clue being supported by means sitting above the other piece

parts.note: loo is an old card game
the FA is the Football Association

explanation.surface: A game is backed by its governing body in a clean-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried plant sponge used for scrubbing in the bath helps one wash.

clue.text: Note distortion of reality in this?

definitions.text: Note distortion of reality in this?

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: a distortion twists the following word's letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A story where reality gets distorted, worth remarking on.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful story of magic is a classic distortion of the real world.

clue.text: Look after stock, regarding old ones unfavourably

definitions.meaning: to take in livestock to graze for payment
prejudiced against the elderly, a variant spelling of ageist

explanation.definitionFit: A legal term for pasturing others' cattle for a fee, and a variant spelling of the word for prejudice against the old.

clue.text: Past master broadcast this on air

indicators.note: broadcast means the letters are scattered and laid out anew

explanation.surface: An expert chooses to transmit this on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of the past is a master of past events.

clue.text: Picked this college, say, to be illustrated

definitions.text: Picked this college, say, to be illustrated

parts.words: Picked this college, say, to be illustrated
parts.note: spoken quickly, the word picked followed by the name of an Oxford college sounds like a word meaning illustrated with pictures

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an Oxford college; 'picked' plus its name, said aloud, gives PICTORIAL, which means illustrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Named Oxford college, whose name after 'picked' gives a word for illustrated.

clue.text: Pain produced by order leading to rows, plain and simple

indicators.note: leading puts the order before the pain in the answer

parts.note: the Garter is the highest English order of chivalry
a stitch is a sharp pain in the side

explanation.surface: An ache brought on by a command to row, pure and simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' and 'plain' are knitting terms: every row is knitted in plain stitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The basic knitting pattern in which every row is plain-knitted.
